newsitem.title: ANGOLA: U.N. envoy allays fears of fresh delay in Angola.
newsitem.headline: U.N. envoy allays fears of fresh delay in Angola.

text.p: The United Nations' special representative in Luanda moved on Thursday to quash growing concerns over another delay in the inauguration of Angola's first peace-time government.

"I want to reassure concerned Angolans, as well as the international community, that the new government will be sworn in on April 11, as was decided last week," U.N. envoy Alioune Blondin Beye told reporters in the capital Luanda.

Beye's declaration follows a communique by the ruling MPLA party earlier this week that the status of former rebel UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi could only be ratified after his movement's 70 deputies joined the National Assembly.

UNITA, which has long insisted that Savimbi's status -- as leader of the largest opposition -- must be decided beforehand, reacted angrily to the MPLA communique, which it said violated the peace accord agreed in 1994.
Western diplomats said the MPLA's statement had caused tensions between the two parties ahead of the ceremony formally establishing Angola's government of national unity.
In a move apparently aimed at calming UNITA's fears, Beye told reporters Savimbi's status would be approved by the National Assembly before UNITA deputies were sworn in.
Beye would not be drawn on the MPLA communique, however, saying: "I don't comment on the declarations of political parties."
The secretariat of Angola's National Assembly confirmed on Thursday evening that Savimbi's status would be discussed by a plenary session on April 8.

The MPLA-led government of President Jose Eduardo dos Santos and Savimbi's UNITA, who fought a civil war for two decades after independence from Portugal in 1975, have delayed the formation of the unity government three times since January 25.
